personas.name: routine-hearing-loss-pure-tone-audiometry-complete
personas.description: Well-formed routine referral: gradual bilateral hearing difficulty, pure-tone audiometry requested (first-line), no red flags, every completeness field present — expect usually-appropriate + routine + low priority + accept.

request.clinicalQuestion: Gradual bilateral hearing difficulty over the past year, worse in noisy environments — assess hearing thresholds.
request.relevantHistory: No occupational noise exposure. No ototoxic medication.

firedRules.description: Requested pure-tone-audiometry test is the recommended examination for "hearing-loss".
No red flags; urgency follows the requested tier (routine).
Routine acuity and an acceptable indication — clinical priority low.

personas.name: emergency-sudden-hearing-loss-within-30-days-high-priority
personas.description: Sudden bilateral hearing loss 3 days ago: pure-tone audiometry is the recommended test for the sudden-hearing-loss indication, and the sudden onset within the past 30 days itself auto-escalates triage to an otological emergency (be seen within 24 hours, per NICE QS185 / ENT-UK) regardless of the routine urgency requested, which independently sets clinical priority to high — expect usually-appropriate + emergency + high priority + accept.

request.clinicalQuestion: Sudden onset bilateral hearing loss 3 days ago, no preceding infection — assess hearing thresholds urgently to guide steroid treatment.
request.relevantHistory: No recent upper respiratory tract infection. Not on ototoxic medication.

triage.notes: ENT on-call aware; time-critical for the steroid treatment window.

firedRules.description: Requested pure-tone-audiometry test is the recommended examination for "sudden-hearing-loss".
Sudden sensorineural hearing loss within the past 30 days — otological emergency; be seen within 24 hours.
Emergency triage tier sets clinical priority high.

flags.description: Sudden onset of hearing loss within the past 30 days — possible sudden sensorineural hearing loss (otological emergency).
flags.suggestedAction: Refer to ENT to be seen within 24 hours; steroid treatment is time-critical (ENT-UK / BAO-HNS).

personas.name: query-referrer-suspected-otosclerosis-other-test-mismatch-unilateral-discharge-incomplete
personas.description: Progressive left-sided hearing loss with intermittent ear discharge: an 'other' test was requested even though tympanometry (with pure-tone audiometry also ideal) is the recommended examination for the suspected-otosclerosis indication, a clear mismatch that forces appropriateness to usually-not-appropriate and the recommendation to query-referrer regardless of completeness; the unilateral symptoms and the ear discharge each independently force urgent triage and moderate clinical priority, and several administrative fields are not yet captured — expect usually-not-appropriate + urgent + moderate priority + query-referrer, completeness below 100.

request.relevantHistory: Progressive left-sided hearing loss over several years with intermittent discharge; family history of otosclerosis.

triage.notes: Query whether tympanometry or PTA is more appropriate; the discharge needs review before testing.

firedRules.description: Requested other test is not usually appropriate for "suspected-otosclerosis"; query the referrer.
Unilateral / asymmetric audiovestibular symptoms — urgent diagnostic referral.
Urgent triage tier sets clinical priority moderate.

flags.description: Unilateral / asymmetric hearing loss, tinnitus, or vertigo reported.
flags.suggestedAction: Refer for ENT / audiovestibular diagnostic assessment to exclude retrocochlear pathology (e.g. vestibular schwannoma).
Arrange ENT review before / alongside testing; tympanometry and pure-tone audiometry may be deferred until the ear is dry.
Query the referrer for the specific question the test should answer.
